full_judgment:
3. Opposite party as defendant contested the suit filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint and stating, inter alia, that the defendant was not liable to be evicted from the suit property in view of Clause-H in the agreement and that the defendant offered rent of December 1992 in favour of the plaintiff but the rent was not accepted nor the rent of January 1993 was accepted by the landlord and the rent being sent to the landlord by money order the defendant filed House Rent Case No. 5 of 1993 and that the defendant was not aware of the transfer of the suit property in favour of the plaintiff and that since the defendant deposited rent in the HR Case No. 5 of 1993 he was not a defaulter. 

 8. It appears that the plaintiff-petitioner filed the suit against the defendant for a decree of ejectment on the grounds that included a ground that the defendant was a defaulter but the specific case of the defendant is that he is not at all a defaulter inasmuch as he deposited rent in the HR Case No. 5 of 1993. From Exhibit 7 judgment dated 29-6-95 passed in HR Case No. 6 of 1995 (previously registered as HR Case No. 5 of 1993) it appears that the said HR Case filed by the defendant-opposite party was rejected by the trial Court. It is submitted on behalf of the defendant that against the aforesaid judgment he preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 151 of 1995. It appears from Annexure 'X' filed by the plaintiff-petitioner along with supplementary affidavit that the said Miscellaneous Appeal has been dismissed on 28-2-96 by the learned District Judge. It further appears that the defendant-opposite party himself in his evidence admitted that the aforesaid Miscellaneous Appeal has been dismissed after hearing the parties. It has been further admitted, categorically by the defendant-opposite party in his evidence that after disposal of both the cases i.e, HR Case No. 5 of 93/6 of 95 and Miscellaneous Appeal No. 151 of 1995 he did not deposit any rent of the suit premises. Without going further deep into the matter it may be held that a tenant is protected from ejectment if he paid rent to the full extent, permissible under the Ordinance and in view of section 18(1) of the House Rent Control Ordinance, it can be said that notwithstanding anything contained in the Transfer of Property Act 1882 or the Contract Act, 1872 no order or decree for recovery of possession can be made against a tenant so long as the tenant paid rent to the full extent allowable by the Ordinance and performs the condition of the tenancy. 

 9. There is no dispute that the Miscellaneous Appeal was dismissed on 28-2-1996 while the suit in question was pending. According to own showing of the defendant, as stated above, it appears that he did not pay any rent whatsoever after the HR Case in question and also since 28-2-1996 i.e. date of disposal of the Miscellaneous Appeal in question. As such, it appears that the defendant's liability for payment of the rent at least before the judgment passed in the suit in question, has not been discharged and the defendant did not pay rent according to his own showing and, therefore, is not protected under the law. It may further be held that once a tenant is a defaulter he is always a defaulter. 

 10. Md Fazlul Karim, learned Advocate for the plaintiff petitioner, referred to the case of Ramijan Ali Mistry vs Md Hedayetullah reported in 31 DLR (AD) 183 wherein the above principle of law has been elaborately discussed and settled. In view of the facts and circumstances and the position of law as decided in 31 DLR case I cannot hold any opinion contrary to the law and find that the defendant opposite party is a defaulter. It is surprising to find that though issue No. 2 was framed by the trial Court for decision as to whether the defendant was a defaulter but nowhere in the judgment there is any finding as to this vital issue. On this ground alone the impugned judgment of the trial Court cannot stand in the eye of law. 

 "That in case of any dispute or differences between the parties to this agreement, an arbitrator may be appointed by representing equal members of either side and any decision made by this arbitrator is binding to the parties to this agreement." 

 14. From the aforesaid clause 'J" it appears that an option was given to the parties for appointment of arbitrator in case of any dispute or difference between the patties o this agreement. 

 16. Learned Advocate for the plaintiff-petitioner submits that even in case of any arbitration clause in the agreement it was the duty of the defendant to resort to section 34 of the Arbitration Act but no such step being taken the point cannot be agitated now. More so, such step by filing application for arbitration could be taken in the Court before filing the written statement. He further submits that there being non fulfillment of obligation by the defendant the plaintiff filed the suit with reference to section 35 of the Arbitration Act and in view of the evidence of plaintiff revealed in his cross-examination that attempts for amicable disposal/ arbitration being made the clause as to arbitration cannot stand as a legal bar against the plaintiff to get a decree in the suit. In view of the facts and circumstances and evidence on record it appears that the submission made by, the learned Advocate of the plaintiff-petitioner is not bereft of substance. In any view of the matter defendant being found to be a defaulter, is not entitled to any protection of ejectment according to provision of Premises Rent Control Ordinance or Transfer of Property Act. As stated above there being no finding whatsoever on this vital point in the impugned judgment I am satisfied that the judgment suffers from illegality.
